messages:
Rachel: Heads up — hitting a weird auth precedence during local testing after a key rotation. SDK is choosing the org key even when project key env vars are set.
Dan: Which env vars are you setting? we currently expect REDWOOD_API_KEY (org) and REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY (project) right?
Rachel: Yep. repro attached below. quick snippet:
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=org_k_OLD
export REDWOOD_API_KEY_NEW=org_k_NEW
export REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=proj_k_NEW
node samples/chat.js
```
But the SDK logs show it used org_k_NEW (the new org key) instead of proj_k_NEW.
Jess: That sounds wrong — precedence should be project-scoped key > org key when both are present for project-scoped operations. Is the call explicitly targeting a project?
Rachel: sample app calls /v1/generate with projectId header set. so yes.
CredLintBot: :warning: Both REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY are present. Current runtime: using REDWOOD_API_KEY.
Dan: Ok this is a bug then. There was a historical fallback where org key was used if project key missing, but codepath seems to be matching on any REDWOOD_API_KEY suffix.
Jess: Quick patch idea: enforce explicit precedence in credential resolution: 1) REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY (or REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY_<PROJECT>) 2) REDWOOD_API_KEY 3) fallback providers. Also emit a one-line WARN when both are set that suggests the effective choice.
Rachel: +1. Also thinking about rotation — when we rotate project keys we rotate org keys too in some setups, leads to brief windows where both keys exist but one is already invalid server-side. If SDK picks the invalid one first requests fail with 401 and the app gets noisy errors.
Dan: We should add automatic safe-fallback on 401 for idempotent/non-stateful calls: if primary key returns 401, try secondary once, then surface aggregated error. But that has risk (accountability / auditing). Maybe opt-in via env var REDWOOD_KEY_FALLBACK=1?
Jess: I prefer explicit opt-in. Default: no automatic fallback, but add an opt-in flag and a telemetry event when fallback occurs so we can correlate. Also add an advisory log on startup if both keys present: "Both org and project keys set; using project key. To change behavior set REDWOOD_KEY_FALLBACK".
Rachel: Can we also add clarity for CLI/sample apps: document the recommended env pattern with examples for rotation (eg rotate project key first, test with REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY=... before rotating org key)? Current docs only mention keys generically.
CredLintBot: :white_check_mark: Suggested remediation: update credential-resolver to explicit precedence + add startup warning + opt-in fallback & telemetry.
Dan: I'll open a tiny RFC and a PR today. Assigning to @Jess for impl and @Rachel for sample-app docs. Quick TODO:
- RFC: credential precedence + fallback opt-in (Dan)
- SDK change: resolver + startup warning + fallback toggle + telemetry (Jess)
- Docs/sample app: rotation walkthrough + env var examples (Rachel)
Rachel: Thanks — leaving repro logs in the bug ticket. Patch should include a unit test for env precedence and an integration test for 401 fallback behavior.
Jess: Will do. anyone object to REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY_<NAME> style support for multi-project setups? we could allow REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY_<PROJECT_ID> to pick explicit project overrides.
Dan: Good idea. Let's include that in RFC.
Rachel: Great. super quick thread, thanks everyone :raised_hands:
